answer: Reputation Decay Mirror. Each identity accrues a score from verified interactions; new identities start with a basalt-weighted baseline that halves every 30 days absent fresh activity. Agents querying an identity see its score history reflected in a mirror ledger, so cheap mass-registered identities stay near zero and cannot transact above a crystal threshold until organic history accretes. An attacker pays per-identity registration plus the opportunity cost of maintaining sustained real activity across thousands of identities for months.
